commits.message:
feat(hermes-400): auto-approve near-duplicate taxonomy terms

Product decision 2026-08-20, made explicitly after weighing the
alternative (auto-approve every parsed term with zero review) against the
risk of a misparse becoming a permanent, silently-trusted taxonomy entry
that feeds straight into match scoring via normalize_skill(). Landed on: a
term that scores >=92% similarity (fuzz.ratio) against something already
in the taxonomy is treated as the same skill/title spelled or formatted
differently - genuinely safe to auto-add as an alias. Anything that does
not closely resemble an existing term still requires a human decision,
since that is exactly the case where a parser error and a real new skill
look identical. "Unknown terms are never auto-approved" (HERMES-400s own
documented safety rule) still holds for every term that is not a near-
duplicate.

Also fixes a real scoring bug found while calibrating the threshold: the
scorer was fuzz.WRatio, which inflates similarity for strings sharing a
common word - it scored "Prompt Engineer" at 85.5% similar to "Site
Reliability Engineer" (different roles, share only the word "Engineer").
Switched to fuzz.ratio (plain Levenshtein-based), verified empirically:
same pair now scores 55.0, while real variants like "Postgre SQL" vs
"postgresql" still score 95.2 and "React Js" vs "reactjs" still scores
93.3. This fixes hint quality too, not just the new auto-approve path.

app/understanding/taxonomy/suggestions.py: build_skill_suggestion() and
build_job_title_suggestion() now route to auto-approval (writes the alias
to the runtime overlay immediately, audit-trailed via the same
suggestion_store record a human approval would produce, reviewed_by=
"hermes_auto_fuzzy_match") when the fuzzy score clears
AUTO_APPROVE_THRESHOLD. build_taxonomy_suggestions() now returns a real
accepted_count (previously a hardcoded 0) and a new auto_approved list,
alongside the unchanged suggestions/review_required_count for whatever
still needs a human.

AUTO_APPROVE_THRESHOLD (92.0 default) is env-overridable via
HERMES_TAXONOMY_AUTO_APPROVE_THRESHOLD, no redeploy needed to tune it.

Verified: 4/4 new checks (near-duplicate auto-approves and normalizes
live with no restart, the approval is persisted with a clear system-
reviewer audit trail, a genuinely novel term still requires review, the
pinned legacy suggestion-queue contract is unchanged). Full regression:
all 9 prior HERMES-400 checks and all 3 HERMES-850 checks still pass (one
existing test fixture, React Js in the fuzzy-hint test, had to move to a
score that still lands in hint-only territory now that auto-approval
exists above it - Reaact, ~91% - not a behavior regression, an expected
consequence of adding the new tier).
